title: Homemade Shakers
strapline: Fill it, seal it, shake it — an instrument you made yourself, and the sound you chose.
intent: Children make their own instruments, discovering that they can create the tools of music, not just play them.
Children explore how different fillings make different sounds — rice whispers, pasta rattles, bells ring.
Children investigate cause and effect and the science of sound as they test and compare their shakers.
Children develop fine-motor control filling, sealing and decorating their instrument.
Children take pride in a made object and then use it to make music, joining process to purpose.
implementation: Offer safe containers — small bottles, tubs, tins with lids — and a choice of fillings: rice, lentils, pasta, bells, sand.
Let children experiment first: fill, shake, listen, tip out, try a different filling and compare.
Talk about the sounds and why they differ: 'the rice is soft and shushy, the pasta is loud and clacky — why?'
Support filling and sealing — funnels help — and make sure lids are firmly secured before shaking.
Offer materials to decorate the finished shaker, so it's truly theirs.
Bring the shakers to a music session and play along, using them to keep the beat and vary the sound.
Extend to comparing loudness and pitch — more filling or less, big container or small — as a sound investigation.
key_questions: Which filling do you think will be the loudest?
How is the rice sound different from the pasta sound?
What happens if you put in more? Or less?
How could you make it seal so nothing falls out?
Can you keep the beat with your shaker?

impact.text: Children make an instrument and use it to make music.
Children compare how different fillings change the sound.
Children explore cause and effect and the science of sound.
Children fill, seal and decorate with fine-motor control.
Children keep a beat and vary sound with their shaker.
Children take pride in the instrument they have made.

enhancements: A sound-comparison table — order the shakers from quietest to loudest.
A range of containers of different sizes and materials to explore pitch.
Other homemade instruments — a shoebox guitar, a drum from a tin.
A recording so children can hear their shaker in the band.
Decorating materials so each shaker is unique.
A 'sound scientist' challenge: which two shakers sound the same?

playing_exploring: Children experiment with fillings and containers to find sounds.
They test, compare and tip out to try again.
active_learning: Children persist to make and seal a shaker they're proud of.
They keep refining the sound until it's the one they wanted.
creating_thinking: Children predict which filling will be loudest, then test it.
They design their instrument and work out how to make it sound right.
